title: Migrate @earendil-works/pi-telemetry -> @oh-my-pi/pi-telemetry by verbatim copy + scope/vitest/private rewrite
one_line: Telemetry is a 957-line zero-dependency LEAF contract package (callback-scoped span context, in-memory reference adapter, reusable adapter conformance suite, ~250 lines of closed-set attribute type machinery); copy all 12 files, strip 16 `.ts` import extensions, swap 2 vitest imports for bun:test, convert one `private` field to `#state`, and re-scope 14 `@earendil-works/` strings — it depends on ZERO of the other 6 new packages, so it is safe to migrate first.
why_copy_not_reimplement: Three concrete reasons, each grounded in a contract a rewrite would lose. (1) The settlement contract is non-obvious and already regression-tested: `RecordedTelemetrySpan.endSequence` is a monotonic counter (memory.ts:98, `span.endSequence = state.nextEndSequence++`) whose only purpose is to prove child-before-parent end ordering even when siblings finish concurrently — the conformance case 'records nested and concurrent child relationships' (conformance.ts:246-272) asserts `second.endSequence < first.endSequence < parent.endSequence` after releasing two children out of order. A rewrite would naturally use a timestamp or a tree walk and lose that proof. (2) Atomicity under hostile payloads: `mergeAttributes` (memory.ts:63-69) copies first, then assigns, so a `Proxy` that throws on the 2nd `ownKeys` cannot half-apply; and every recording method is individually wrapped in try/catch (memory.ts:143,152,159) so telemetry can never break the caller. The suite proves this with a 4-trap throwing `Proxy` helper (`unreadable()`, conformance.ts:43-58) and asserts the pre-existing bag survives verbatim (conformance.ts:206-218). Rewriting this correctly is exactly the kind of thing that looks right and is subtly wrong. (3) `src/testing/conformance.ts` (315 lines, 9 grouped cases) is not a test file — it is a PUBLISHED export (`./testing` subpath) that third-party adapter authors run against their own backend. It is a product. Reimplementing means re-deriving 9 cases plus the Proxy harness with no reference to check against, and the result would be less useful to the ecosystem than the original. Additionally, on the legal axis the MIT terms make copy cheap and a 'clean-room' rewrite strictly riskier: rewriting is only safe if you never read the source, and this spec's whole premise is that we read it. Copy + preserved notice is the compliant path; a rewrite invites a provenance argument nobody needs to have.

collisions.resolution: KEEP ALL THREE, in a strict dependency order: (1) `@oh-my-pi/pi-telemetry` = the vendor-neutral CONTRACT — zero I/O, zero vendor, zero network, just 'what a span is'. (2) `packages/agent/src/telemetry.ts` = the omp EMITTER that binds that contract to OTEL/OTLP. (3) `packages/stats` = the LOCAL READER that turns session logs into a dashboard. Stats is local (nothing leaves the machine); agent telemetry is remote (OTLP); pi telemetry is neither — it is the vocabulary the other two will eventually share. The integration point is `RecordedTelemetrySpan` (memory.ts:16): it is the normalized shape any omp emitter must produce to be covered by `createTelemetryAdapterConformance`, which is how OTEL and in-memory become provably equivalent. Do NOT port pi's emitter into omp's OTEL file and do NOT make stats depend on telemetry yet — wiring the contract into omp's agent is the AGENT spec's job, not telemetry's.

test_contract: Two test files, both rewritten to bun:test, both contract-level (no source-grep, no mock.module, no tautologies). test/telemetry.test.ts must defend three observable contracts: (a) TYPED SCHEMA EXACTNESS — `defineTelemetrySchema` returns its argument identity, the definition survives `JSON.stringify`, and 5 `@ts-expect-error` blocks prove the closed set: required event attributes cannot be omitted, a value outside a declared `values` list is rejected, an undeclared event name is rejected, and an empty `endAttributes` rejects every attribute. A consumer who regresses this ships spans with misspelled or undeclared attribute keys and no runtime check will ever catch it. (b) VOCABULARY COMBINATION AND CHILD BINDING — `createTypedSpanStarter` over two schemas with disjoint span names resolves to 42 with a `parentId` chain operation->request, and 5 more `@ts-expect-error` blocks prove duplicate span names across schemas, union-valued names, and cross-schema attribute mismatch are all compile errors. (c) NO-OP PASSTHROUGH — the frozen span is admitted synchronously, a child `startSpan` returns the SAME span object, and rejection values are preserved by identity for both sync throws and async rejections. test/conformance.test.ts must drive the 9 published conformance cases against `InMemoryTelemetryContext` under bun:test (proving the suite is runner-portable, which is the suite's entire raison d'etre) plus one extra case for DETACHED SNAPSHOTS: mutating a returned snapshot's `attributes.tags` and `events[0].attributes.value` must not affect the next `getSpans()` call, and `settled`/`endSequence` must transition from `false`/`undefined` to `true`/`1` across the awaited `startSpan`. AGENTS.md bans bare `not.toThrow()` and 'the code ran' assertions, so step 8's 5 replacements are mandatory, not stylistic.
verification: The gate is `bun run check:ts` from /Users/tranquangdang21/Projects/ultraworkers, exit 0, ~29s on an idle machine. It runs `oxlint . && oxfmt --check` over packages/* then `tsgo --noEmit` per package via `--filter './packages/*' --if-present check:types`, so it covers all 4 enforcement layers at once: lint rules, formatter conformance on the copied files, full typecheck of the new package's src+test (including the 11 `@ts-expect-error` assertions, which fail the build if they stop erroring), and every existing package's regression. `bun test` is BLOCKED in this environment (native addon unbuilt; `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` needs `brew install ninja` first), so the two test files are typechecked but not executed at gate time. That is an accepted, disclosed gap: the 9 conformance cases and 4 test cases are contract-level assertions that were green in pi under vitest, and the migration changes only the import line and 7 assertion forms — no production logic. The runner-portability claim (vitest -> bun:test) is therefore NOT empirically proven until `bun test packages/telemetry/` runs on a machine with ninja installed. Re-run the spec's gate as: `bun test packages/telemetry/ && bun run check:ts`. effort: Small. ~1 hour. 12 files / 62831 bytes, of which only 8 files (34128 bytes) contain code. The rewrite surface is 16 specifier extensions, 2 runner imports, 3 `#state` edits, 2 barrel files, 7 assertion edits, 3 manifest files, and 2 registration lines in the root package.json. No new dependency, no build-graph change, no consumer to update — telemetry is a leaf with no dependents inside omp yet, so nothing else in the repo can break. The only genuinely slow part is reading pi's README closely enough to rewrite its integration section honestly for omp's telemetry/agent/stats triad.
risk: LOW, and low in a specific way worth naming: this package has ZERO existing consumers in omp. Nothing imports TelemetryContext, InMemoryTelemetryContext, or any schema type anywhere in the 17-package tree (verified: 0 refs for 33 of the 36 public symbols). So the blast radius of a mistake is confined to packages/telemetry itself and cannot regress the CLI. The real risks are all local and all mechanical: (1) forgetting one of the 16 `.ts` extensions -> TS5097, caught by the gate; (2) leaving `private` in memory.ts -> caught by review and by the `#state`/this.#state mismatch; (3) the vitest->bun:test swap assuming bun lacks `expectTypeOf` -> it has it, verified at packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-runner.test.ts:5; (4) LEGAL, the only unrecoverable one: copying without packages/telemetry/LICENSE carrying Mario Zechner's copyright and full permission notice. That is why it is step 1 and not a step 15 afterthought. A secondary, forward-looking risk: this package introduces `AttributeValue`, `SpanOptions` and `SpanStatus` into a repo that already has same-named OTEL types. Nothing breaks today because neither is re-exported by an omp barrel, but a future `export * from "@oh-my-pi/pi-telemetry"` inside packages/agent/src/index.ts would create an ambiguous star export against the existing `export * from "./telemetry"` at index.ts:24. The resolution is recorded in the collisions table and must be carried into the agent spec.
